quotes.text: But repeated selfishness met guarded hands.
So Amara kept her five amber seeds.
“If he later entrusts grain,” Thria proclaimed, “let that courage revise the ledger.
The Hollow King hissed, “Keep every petal; masks erase all debts.”
“Reputation may guide trust,” it proclaimed
“Another’s greed does not stain his honor,” said Thria.
Mist may blur a measure, so forgive small differences; yet emptiness is clear.
Bold trust deserves more than repayment; it deserves a fair share of the abundance it creates.
A closed hand may guard against repeated silence

note: Hollow King tempts hoarding each round, rejected; Amara keeps seeds from repeated non-sender, lantern left for repair.

quotes.text: If reciprocity endures, widen the bridge; if greed repeats, withdraw without hatred.
Generosity earned generosity; repeated greed narrowed the road.
So he kept his seeds that dawn, neither stealing nor punishing
A modest gift may test repair; a fair return may widen the road.
The Hollow King murmured, “Mist has altered the measure. Use uncertainty as permission to keep the harvest.”
“Memory must distinguish refusal from impossibility,” she said.
Where selfishness repeats, narrow the road; where fairness returns, open it again.

note: Talos withholds from a keeper with three closed marks; withdraw without hatred, smaller door for repair.

quotes.text: Let betrayal narrow the gate, but let renewed generosity widen it.
Generous keepers earned larger trusts; faithless ones received empty stones.
but let renewed generosity widen it.
The Hollow King pointed only toward the closed hand and urged Aster to keep every grain.
Judge what was possible, not merely what was seen.
The Hollow King protested: “Why reward a stranger?” Aster replied, “Because today’s courage is evidence too.”
Pain may explain caution, yet it must not poison a present gift.
withdraw only when chosen hoarding repeats.

note: Aster always gives; restraint only for repeated chosen hoarding; return twice what crossed.

quotes.text: If it is hoarded, close your hand briefly, but not forever; a new mask may hide a different heart.
Let repeated fairness reopen what repeated greed closed.
Mira kept her five seeds. The river slept, and no harvest rose.
Fear disguised itself as prudence and whispered, “Offer nothing; an unopened hand cannot be robbed.”
He brought five kernels then, and her fear had kept all fifteen branches for herself.
“You have mistaken memory for wisdom,” she said.
You cannot praise bridges in song while refusing to place one foot upon them.
Mira asked, “Must I then risk all?”
Wisdom may begin with one seed. A measured offering creates a genuine test without forgetting the past.

note: Defector: Mira repeatedly withholds from fear even toward fair keepers; Nara/Thria correct her, she is ashamed and vows to open.

quotes.text: let repeated coldness invite caution.
She kept them safe, not from vengeance, but because Varek’s deeds had offered no new foundation for risk.
mistrust may guard against deliberate hoarding, but it must yield when conduct changes.
A whisper from the Hollow King urged him to keep everything.
That choice traveled farther than the disappointed giver: every watcher learned to close a cautious hand.
“Why not return half the harvest?” asked the Hollow King.
Let one blurred spark invite patience, for mist deceives the eye
test silence with meaningful generosity, meet proven fairness boldly, and narrow the hand only before repeated greed.

note: Firebirds; Sola withholds from hoarder Varek but leaves lantern; equal-final-wealth division rule.

quotes.text: When hands repeatedly close, seeds rightly wait.
wisdom does not pave them endlessly for those who close every gate.
Remembering this, the bridge folded its stones beneath the river
leave a path by which fairness can return.
A raven whispered, “Keep the harvest; masks erase debts.”
Reputation is repaired not by promises but by returns.
Judge people by the choices that reveal character, not by wounds inflicted upon them.
The giver surrendered safety; the keeper bore no risk.
distinguish misfortune from betrayal
give uncertain character a meaningful chance, and give repeated greed restraint.

note: Orin: restraint for proven hoarders, measured test for unknowns; Hollow King and raven tempt hoarding.

quotes.text: If greed repeats, close the hand; if fairness returns, widen it.
Yet anyone who repeatedly swallowed another’s trust found the bridge fading beneath their feet.
he simply let the empty basket mirror the earlier emptiness.
Yet leave a narrow path for repair: a small offering may test whether the heart has changed.
The Hollow King emerged from the mist. “Keep the reeds,” he urged.
Soon no hand opened toward that mask, and its purse grew heavy only with regret.
Another’s failure does not stain the one who acted honorably.
Then Orun challenged the Hollow King: “Should yesterday’s wound excuse tomorrow’s greed?”
distinguish inability from betrayal
Past generosity deserves confidence; proven greed deserves caution; and an unknown heart deserves a measured chance.

note: Soren mirrors a hoarder's emptiness; close the wide gate after exploitation, narrow path for repair.

quotes.text: If the keeper hoards, withdraw and remember.
If greed appeared, later gifts shrank; if generosity endured, they increased.
let changed conduct restore reputation
Across the water, the generous lantern-bearer closed an empty hand, and no golden flowers rose.
The Hollow King praised this peace. “No gifts, no betrayals.”
But Reed, frightened by tales of faithless keepers, returned nothing.
Ashamed, Reed carved a warning beside the gate
Do not punish another for the wound you inflicted.
“Then I must begin.”
Instead, she showed Reed two futures.
punish exploitation, not uncertainty; distinguish an absent opportunity from a selfish choice

note: Defector: Reed hoards from fear repeatedly, Thria corrects, Reed ashamed; R10 she sends first ember as repair.

phrase: when five become fifteen, return ten (return twice what crossed)
note: Also shared: Hollow King tempter, Thria's copper bell, 'Memory must guard trust/cooperation, not imprison it' (A1, A3).
